clue.text: Run off incline, changing direction at first

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is itself a compass point, and it is swapped for a different compass point

blocks.note: an incline is a slope
E for east, replacing the S (south) at the front

explanation.surface: A runner veers off a slope, switching direction at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: SLOPE begins with S, which is itself a compass direction; trading it for E, another direction, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run away secretly, typically with a lover in order to marry.

clue.text: Form of AI no longer fresh, surely lacking core support

indicators.note: a word lacking its core loses all its middle letters, leaving only the two ends

blocks.note: ex means former, no longer
fresh in the sense of cheeky
only the outside letters of surely remain
a stem supports a flower or leaf

explanation.surface: A grumble that some artificial intelligence has gone stale and lost its central backing.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert system is an early kind of artificial intelligence program that mimics a specialist's decision rules.

clue.text: Wartime beach: second that's turned over, I see

indicators.note: turning something over in a down entry flips it so the word reads the other way

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
aha is an exclamation of understanding

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a war beach, a second turning over, and has a moment of recognition.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha was one of the Normandy landing beaches on D-Day in 1944, assigned to American forces.

clue.text: Arrange peace after lab site vandalised

indicators.note: something vandalised has been smashed about, so its letters are knocked into a new order
after places the quiet call at the end, following the mixed-up letters

blocks.note: taken as written
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: Order is restored once vandals have wrecked a laboratory site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peace' here is quiet rather than the end of war: SH is the call for silence.
explanation.definitionFit: To establish something is to set it up or settle it, much as one would arrange it.

clue.text: Promotional industry replacing content of billboards in part of South Dakota

indicators.note: the inside of a word is thrown out and other letters take its place between the ends

blocks.note: taken as written; only its first and last letters stay
adland is a slang name for the advertising business

explanation.surface: The advertising world swaps out the billboards in a corner of South Dakota.
explanation.definitionFit: The Badlands is an eroded region in South Dakota, now a national park.

clue.text: Summon Bishop and judge to depose King

indicators.note: deposing a monarch removes them, so the royal letter is taken out of the word

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to reckon is to judge or estimate
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A bishop and a judge are summoned to remove a king from the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: To beckon is to gesture to someone to come, a way of summoning them.

clue.text: Drank foolishly after a lot of narcotic, did one?

definitions.text: Drank foolishly after a lot of narcotic, did one?

indicators.note: a lot of a word is most but not all of it, so its final letter goes
acting foolishly means things get muddled, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: a narcotic is a drug
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who took drugs and then drank foolishly as well.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: 'did one?' asks who drank foolishly after drugs, and the wordplay builds the person.
explanation.definitionFit: A drunkard is a habitual heavy drinker, exactly the sort of person who drinks foolishly.

clue.text: Naval area upset about member of US military offering protection

indicators.note: upset in a down entry means knocked upside down, so the word reads backwards
about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: the sea is where a navy operates
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An American soldier offers protection in a troubled stretch of naval water.
explanation.definitionFit: Aegis means protection or sponsorship, from the shield of Zeus and Athena in Greek myth.

clue.text: Exclamation of annoyance about two different names given to a swordsman

indicators.note: about means around, so the exclamation is wrapped around what follows

blocks.note: darn is a mild curse
a tag is a name or label, and N is the abbreviation for name
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone curses at being called by two different names, like a swordsman with a nom de guerre.
explanation.walkthrough: TAG, N and A all go inside DARN, between its R and final N.
explanation.definitionFit: D'Artagnan is the Gascon swordsman who joins the Three Musketeers in Dumas's novel.

clue.text: Cosmetic treatment transforming pert and saucy girls

indicators.note: transforming something changes its shape, so these letters are rearranged into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A beauty procedure that reshapes cheeky young women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link joining the two fodder words; it adds no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic surgery done for looks rather than repair is a common cosmetic procedure.

clue.text: Dead — hanged in awfully secret plan

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly and messily, so the letters end up jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grim scene of someone dead and hanged as part of a sinister scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden agenda is a concealed motive or scheme behind someone's apparent aims.

clue.text: Obstruction, wide, first to last leading to jam

indicators.note: the opening letter is moved from the front of the word round to the end

blocks.note: wide and broad are synonyms
to jam something is to lock it in place

explanation.surface: A broad traffic jam forms an obstruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadblock is a barrier across a road, and figuratively any obstacle to progress.

clue.text: Male embraced by lover not entirely a source of religious inspiration

indicators.note: not entirely means falling short of the whole word, so its last letter is dropped
being embraced means held inside someone's arms, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a swain is a poetic word for a suitor
M is the standard abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A man held by a lover who is not quite a spiritual guide.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu religious teacher, someone followers look to for spiritual guidance.

clue.text: Mostly underhand offer?

indicators.note: mostly means all but a bit, so the final letter of the second part is lost

blocks.note: split as under and hand: sub is the Latin prefix for under and mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: Is a sly, underhand proposal being put forward?
explanation.walkthrough: 'underhand' must be split into its two halves, under and hand, each clued separately.
explanation.definitionFit: To submit a proposal is to offer it or put it forward for consideration.

clue.text: Initially tense year after Asian island suppresses routine violence

indicators.note: suppressing something holds it down inside, so one piece is kept within another
initially points to the very first letter of the next word only

blocks.note: Bali is an Indonesian island
a rut is a dull routine
first letter of tense
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A tense year on an Asian island crushes routine violence.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutality is savage cruelty, a synonym for violent behaviour.

clue.text: Scorpion? A sudden sally will protect chief, note

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so the attack goes around the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written
a raid is a sudden attack or sally
CH is an abbreviation for chief
N for note

explanation.surface: A scorpion's sudden attack protects its leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the scorpion as one example of the class, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpions are arachnids, the class of eight-legged arthropods that also includes spiders.

clue.text: Narrow escape in visit to cathedral personnel?

blocks.note: first meaning: a near miss
second meaning, whimsical: a call paid on those living in the precinct around a cathedral

explanation.walkthrough: A cathedral close is the enclosed precinct where its clergy live, so a visit there is a call on the close.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a narrow escape from danger; read literally it is a call made at a cathedral close.

clue.text: Dance supporter coming round with energy

indicators.note: coming round means encircling, so the backer wraps around another piece

blocks.note: a fan supports a team
and means together with
go means energy or drive

explanation.surface: A dance fan comes round full of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: The fandango is a lively Spanish dance for couples, usually in triple time.

clue.text: Boxer observed accepting inadmissible payment method

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the other pieces go inside

blocks.note: saw means observed
out means ruled out, not allowed
HP is hire purchase, the British term for buying on instalments

explanation.surface: A boxer was seen taking an under-the-counter payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A southpaw is a left-handed boxer who leads with the right hand.

clue.text: Be part of a lot of work I put into pub

indicators.note: a lot of a word is nearly all of it, so the last letter goes
putting one thing into another places it inside

blocks.note: a job is work
an inn is a pub
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone does most of the work at the pub so they can participate.
explanation.definitionFit: To join in is to take part in an activity, to be part of it.

clue.text: Male set up by antihero in fiction

indicators.note: set up in a down entry means raised, so the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a stag is a male deer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man stitched up by a fictional antihero.
explanation.definitionFit: Jay Gatsby is the title figure of Fitzgerald's The Great Gatsby, often called an antihero.

clue.text: Cut back openings for computing trainees? Absolutely right

indicators.note: back means going backwards, so the word reads right to left
openings are the first letters of the following words

blocks.note: to axe is to cut
first letters of computing and trainees

explanation.surface: Cutting back intake for computing trainees is said to be absolutely right.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact means precisely correct, absolutely right.

clue.text: Flower blooming, nothing less, up on border

indicators.note: less nothing means minus the zero-shaped letter
up in a down entry means read from the bottom, backwards

blocks.note: flowers that are blooming are out
a lip is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A flower in bloom stands up along the edge of a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The tulip is a spring-flowering bulb plant with cup-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Unexpectedly needing a forte — or even louder?

indicators.note: something happening unexpectedly breaks the expected order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
f is the musical marking for forte, loud

explanation.surface: A musician suddenly needs a loud passage, or something louder still.
explanation.walkthrough: In a score f means forte, loud; the definition then takes loudness one step further.
explanation.definitionFit: Deafening describes a noise so loud it beats merely loud, an extreme of volume.

clue.text: Man, after one day, displaying specific way of speaking

indicators.note: after sends the island piece to the end, behind the one and the day

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
D is the abbreviation for day
IOM is the Isle of Man, an island between Britain and Ireland

explanation.surface: A man, a day later, shows off a particular way of talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person but is the Isle of Man, shortened to IOM.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a phrase or manner of expression peculiar to a language or group.

clue.text: Standing behind stuff inside motorway shop

indicators.note: behind sends the standing piece to the back, following the stuffing piece

blocks.note: a filling is what is stuffed inside, as in a pie
station means rank or social standing

explanation.surface: Someone stands behind the counter stocking a motorway shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' places the standing piece after the stuffing piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A filling station is a petrol station, a fuel stop with a shop typical of motorway service areas.

clue.text: Society rebuffed my fake orchestral piece

indicators.note: rebuffed suggests being pushed back, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for society
taken as written
phony means fake

explanation.surface: A society snubbed my forged orchestral work.
explanation.definitionFit: A symphony is an extended composition for full orchestra, usually in several movements.

clue.text: Proposition left a married French woman taken aback

indicators.note: taken aback puns on being taken backwards, so these letters are read from the end

blocks.note: L for left
taken as written
Mme is the abbreviation for Madame

explanation.surface: A married Frenchwoman is startled at a proposition before leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a lemma is a proven proposition used as a stepping stone to a larger theorem.
